sections.content: How many people stayed in Oldham after gaining qualifications?

Oldham is a large town in the North West. Oldham does not have its own university.

Oldham has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Oldham ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 5,540 state-school pupils from Oldham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,430 (26%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,590 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Oldham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Oldham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Oldham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Oldham move to?

Of Oldham's graduates, 300 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 170 of those graduates (57%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Oldham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 355 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 255 of those qualified non-graduates (72%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Oldham's GCSE cohort:

  • 115 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was Yorkshire and The Humber
  • 85 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 15% of graduates and 19% of qualified non-graduates living in Oldham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,295 graduates and 1,480 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Oldham. This is compared with the 1,430 graduates and 1,590 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 85% of the graduates had also lived in Oldham as GCSE pupils, while 15% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Oldham in 2018 to 2019, 81% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 19% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
